q: 1. The artificial activity which indicates that an activity following it, cannot be started unless the preceding activity is complete, is known as
explain: A dummy activity is an artificial, zero-duration link used to enforce correct dependency/precedence relationships in the network.

q: 2. In a time-cost optimization using CPM the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: To reduce project duration most economically, we crash the critical activity that has the lowest cost slope (cheapest to crash first).

q: 3. A dummy activity
options: is represented by a dotted line
explain: A dummy activity is artificially introduced, shown as a dotted arrow, and consumes no time - all characteristics apply.

q: 4. The amount of time required performing any event in case of PERT should be ................... CPM.
explain: Because PERT deals with uncertain/probabilistic time estimates and CPM uses deterministic ones, the actual time required can vary based on the nature of the project.

q: 5. The estimated time required to perform an activity, is known as
explain: Duration is the estimated time needed to complete an activity.

q: 6. PERT technique of network analysis is useful for
explain: PERT is ideally suited for Research and Development projects where the duration of activities is uncertain and has not been performed before.

q: 7. The difference between the time available to do a job and the time required to do the job, is known as
explain: Float (slack) is defined as the difference between available time and required time for completing an activity.

q: 8. Latest start of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The latest start time of an activity must be less than or equal to the latest allowable event time at its preceding node to avoid delaying the project.

q: 9. PERT means
options: pertinent programming related to a project
explain: PERT is the standard acronym for Program Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 10. The critical activity has
explain: By definition, a critical activity has zero total float, since any delay would push back the overall project completion.

q: 11. PERT is
explain: PERT focuses on milestones or 'events' (reaching a specific stage), whereas CPM focuses on the 'activities' or tasks themselves.

q: 12. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as
explain: Free float is the amount of delay possible in an activity without affecting the earliest start of any succeeding activity.

q: 13. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: In the context of network analysis, waiting is considered a 'dummy activity' or an activity because it consumes time, even if it doesn't consume physical resources.

q: 14. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents
explain: The critical path determines the minimum time in which the entire project can be completed.

q: 15. Which one of the following represents an activity
explain: All listed tasks (curing concrete, setting a question paper, preparing breakfast) are processes that take time and resources, hence all represent activities.

q: 16. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' denotes a completed state/milestone (an instantaneous occurrence), representing an event rather than an ongoing process.

q: 17. Critical path lies along the activities having total float
explain: Activities on the critical path always have zero total float by definition.

q: 18. The benefit of the PERT network is taken by the management in
options: readjusting the time to meet the target
explain: PERT provides a comprehensive framework for scheduling, inter-departmental coordination, and dynamic readjustment based on probability.

q: 19. The time which result in the least possible construction cost of an activity, is known
explain: (May be wrong )As per book Normal time is the duration at which the activity's direct cost is minimum (most economical execution pace).

q: 20. Which of the following time estimate is related to PERT?
explain: PERT uses a 'three-time estimate' approach (Optimistic, Pessimistic, and Most Likely) to account for uncertainty.

q: 21. If t0, tp and tm are the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates of an activity respectively, the expected time t of the activity will be
explain: The PERT expected time formula is te = (t0 + 4tm + tp)/6, giving greatest weight to the most likely time.

q: 22. The event which act as head as well as tail for different activities is, called
explain: An internal node in a network that marks the finish of one activity and the start of another is a dual role event.

q: 23. The figure below is used to indicate (merge symbol where multiple arrows converge into one node)
explain: When multiple activity arrows converge into a single node, this is called a merge event.

q: 24. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using the PERT formula $t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6$: $(1 + 4(3) + 11) / 6 = 24 / 6 = 4$ days.

q: 25. The figure below is used to indicate (burst symbol where one node diverges into multiple arrows)
explain: When a single node diverges into multiple activity arrows, this is called a burst event.

q: 26. Of the following, the PERT event is
explain: Events are instantaneous milestones. 'Concrete cured' signifies a finished state (event), whereas the others are ongoing processes (activities).

q: 27. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known
explain: Critical ratio scheduling is the specific technique used to set and maintain job priorities based on time remaining versus work remaining.

q: 28. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis relies on all three time estimates to calculate the expected mean time.

q: 29. PERT is
options: used for research and development projects
based on three time estimates for activities linking up two events
explain: PERT is event-oriented, commonly used for R&D projects with uncertain durations, and relies on three time estimates linking events - all statements are true.

q: 30. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Events are graphically represented as circles or rectangles, commonly referred to as nodes in a network diagram.

q: 31. CPM is
options: is built of activities oriented programme
explain: CPM synthesizes project activities into an integrated program, is activity-oriented, and suits repetitive construction-type work - all apply.

q: 32. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time in PERT is
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) in a normal distribution represents the 50% probability mark (the mean).

q: 33. CPM family includes
explain: The CPM family of techniques includes Critical Path Analysis, Critical Path Plotted diagrams, and Critical Path Scheduling variants - all the above.

q: 34. The slack for an event i is given by
explain: Event slack is given by the difference between latest allowable time and earliest expected time[cite: 1].

q: 35. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are
explain: A probability factor (Z-score) of zero means the scheduled time equals the expected time, resulting in a 50% chance of success.

q: 36. In CPM analysis,
explain: CPM emphasizes activities, assumes deterministic (certain) durations, and represents activities as arrows - all statements are correct.

q: 37. Variance is
options: Sum of time duration for various job / number of jobs
difference between the time under consideration and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviation
explain: Variance is defined statistically as the mean of squared deviations[cite: 1].

q: 38. You are going to design a new computer programme, which would you like to prefer?
explain: Software development involves high uncertainty in task durations, making the probabilistic PERT method more suitable than deterministic CPM.

q: 39. Bar chart is used for minor project, CPM is used for repetitive work while PERT is used for
options: limited time and unlimited resources types of work
uncertainty time and resources types of work
explain: PERT is specifically designed for non-repetitive projects where time and resource requirements are uncertain.

q: 40. In PERT analysis the actual performance of task is known as
explain: The actual work or performance required to progress from one event to another is termed an activity.

q: 41. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: PERT assumes activity time estimates follow a Beta distribution, which allows for skewness between optimistic and pessimistic estimates.

q: 42. Line of balance technique is used for
options: comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Line of Balance (LOB) is a management control process used for highly repetitive projects to compare actual progress against the plan.

q: 43. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: the office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' is a state/point in time (an event), not a time-consuming activity like the other options.

q: 44. In PERT, optimistic time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Optimistic time ($t_o$) assumes everything goes perfectly, representing the minimum possible duration.

q: 45. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total float is calculated as the difference between an activity's latest start time and its earliest start time (or equivalently, LFT - EFT).

q: 46. In PERT, pessimistic time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Pessimistic time ($t_p$) assumes everything goes wrong (excluding major disasters), representing the maximum duration.

q: 47. If TL is the latest allowable event occurrence time, total activity slacks (S), is equal to
explain: Total float/slack can be equivalently computed as LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or TL-EFT, all giving the same result - so all of the above is correct.

q: 48. In PERT, the most likely time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: The most likely time ($t_m$) is the duration that would occur most frequently if the activity were repeated many times.

q: 49. All the following are valid for CPM except
options: the beginning and end of an activity is denoted by nodes
explain: CPM assumes deterministic, certain activity durations; allowing uncertainties is NOT valid for CPM (that characteristic belongs to PERT).

q: 50. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is equal to
explain: The weighted average (expected time) in PERT is calculated using the formula $(a + 4m + b) / 6$.
